My name is Robert Allen Rusk and I am a hardcore gamer with about 30+ years
of gaming experience. I am an ex-gametester (Broderbund Software, LucasArts
Games, Point Of View Computing) and an ex-arcade attendant (Namco
Cyberstation - Pier 39, San Francisco, CA). I also own multiple systems such
as the Sega Dreamcast, Super Nintendo, Nintendo 64, Atari Jaguar, PlayStation
(1, 2, and 3), Original Xbox, and Xbox 360.

I started writing guides in 2003 because I felt it was something I could do
utilizing my writing skills gained in college and gametesting along with my
passion for vidgames. Over time I have honed my overall writing and
organization skills plus my creative thinking skills. Additionally, I have
extended the play value of the games I have written guides and FAQs for many
times over plus I have received many letters from all over the world.

I am also what one may call an RGB Analog Video enthusiast. I hack most of my
game consoles to try to get the best possible video from them and that
usually involves tapping into the RGB Analog video signals and using them on
the right monitors to achieve my desires. To this end I became a member of
the GamesX.com mod forum and I post on their "RGB + Video Discussions" forum
area from time to time.

In addition, I am a member of the X-Otic Computer Systems of San Antonio
(www.xcssa.org), a group who specializes in Linux, Mac, and other systems. We
are also a group of hackers and electronics enthusiasts.

I am also a regular forum poster at GameFAQs, an occasional poster at
AtariAge, Digital Press, GTA Forums, and Video Game Saga. I am also a member
of The MoFaT (a members only message board set up by "Grand Theft Auto: Vice
City" players who met on the Vice City message boards at GameFAQs).

Outside of gaming, my interests include "Godzilla" (I have been a G-Fan since
the age of ten) and "Red Dwarf". I am also a long time soundtrack collector
with many titles in my possession. As far as favorite sports teams go, my
teams are the San Antonio Spurs (NBA) [the local team], the Denver Broncos
(NFL) [although I live in Texas, I am originally from Colorado Springs,
Colorado] and the Air Force Falcons (NCAA Football).

This guide was constructed using TextWrangler on an Apple Mac Mini. I view my
work in Safari to help in seeing how it would look on the web and correct
format errors.

 /=========================================================================\
| >GEN1. About The Guide                                                    |
 \=========================================================================/
            \=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=/

Welcome to my "Grand Theft Auto V" guide! In this document you will find a
lot of useful information in a highly organized format that you can use to
beat all of the missions of the game. Quotes taken from readers' e-mail are
presented "as is" and may include spelling and grammatical errors.

The main emphasis of this guide is to provide creative and simple solutions 
to many of the missions in the game. I have worked hard to make sure that
this guide is as complete as possible  but at the same time leave room for
exploration. I hope that you enjoy this guide as much as learn from it.

While this guide was written initially for the Xbox 360 version of the game,
it should also benefit those with the PS3 version. If any of the strategies
in this guide won't work in the PS3 version then feel free to write me and
let me know so I can make additional adjustments in future revisions.

Although there are some new weapons that are made available through DLC this
guide is written with the base weapons provided through the Main Story.

Another emphasis of this guide is *ORDER*. If you do the missions and tasks
in a certain order then the game will be easier and more fun for you. You
don't absolutely have to do them in the order I have suggested but, as you
read the guide, you will see how it benefitted me.

Each collectible and activity has a letter designation to make them easier to
identify in this guide. In addition, there is a three letter Region Prefix
(listings below) indicating a particular area where the item or activity can
be found (in these examples I use "XXX"):

  >>Stunt Jumps will be identified with an "J".
      --Example: Jump XXX-J21.

  >>Bridges will be identified with an "B".
      --Example: Bridge XXX-B19.

  >>Knife Flights will be identified with an "KF".

  >>Letter Scraps will be identified with an "LS".
      --Example: Scrap XXX-LS46.

  >>Spaceship Parts will be identified with an "SP".
      --Example: Part XXX-SP47.

  >>Nuclear Waste will be identified with an "NT"

0================0
| Region Prefixes \
0=====================================>

  BLC - Blaine County
  LCY - Los Santos County
  LSO - Los Santos

 /=========================================================================\
| >GEN2. Grand Theft Auto V                                                 |
 \=========================================================================/
            \=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=/

GTA V is the most ambitious title that Rockstar Games has ever produced. It
has also shattered sales records with amazing speed. It features three
protagonists and has a very large map that covers a variety of terrain in
including a fantastic underwater world. The story focuses on heists and the
lives of the three "amigos" that pull them off. Although this is an awesome
game it does have some flaws.

Because of the three protagonists the story seems to feel a bit unfocused and
the Cops are probably the toughest of all the GTAs (although once you get
better weapons and upgrade certain Skills then they will be easier to deal
with).

The radio is also a mixed bag (you could say the same of most of the other
installments) with some glaring omissions (lack of a metal station and a new
age station given the involvement of Tangerine Dream on the soundtrack).

With that said let's look over the game in detail.....

            /=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=\
 /=========================================================================\
| >GEN3. Game Installation and Technical Data                               |
 \=========================================================================/
            \=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=/

Because GTA V is a very large game you will need to install it to hard drives
and/or flash drives before being allowed to play. Below are install data and
other technical information:

0=========0
| Xbox 360 \
0====================================================>

  This version comes on two discs. One of them must be installed onto a a 
  hard drive and the other must be played using at least the DVD-ROM drive. 
  But you should not install both discs to the hard drive. According to 
  Rockstar, because of how the game is programmed, you need to read the data 
  from two different sources. Otherwise glitches and other problems may 
  appear.

  Thankfully you can use flash drives on the X360 and install one of the 
  discs there if you do not wish to use the DVD-ROM drive. Based on 
  information from various forums it is best to use a flash drive with a high 
  transfer rate and install the Install disc to it. Then install the Play 
  disc to the hard drive. You still need to put the disc into the DVD-ROM 
  drive but this is mainly for verification purposes.

  The game will recognize multiple sources of game save data (HDD, Memory 
  Unit, USB Drive) and you can switch between them if needed. However, you 
  can only save fifteen saves to a device. If you wish to archive multiple 
  saves then you will need multiple devices.

0==============0
| PlayStation 3 \
0====================================================>

  This version, which is a single large capacity Blu-Ray disk, can be easily 
  installed onto the console's hard drive. However, only 8GB will actually be 
  installed - the remainder of the game remains on the disc and can only be 
  played from the Blu-Ray drive. As a result, game loading and reloading is 
  much slower than the Xbox 360 version.

  The game will only recognize one source of game save data (HDD). You can 
  still archive saves to other devices such as an SD Card but it must be done 
  at the dashboard.

  Although it looks like you could archive a lot of saves to a single 
  external device the machine will only allow you to save fifteen saves to 
  one (just like the Xbox 360 version). In order to use an archived save you 
  must overwrite a save on the HDD while at the dashboard before starting the 
  game.

  Transferring game saves from one machine to another, such as in the case of 
  machine failure, can be problematic. To prevent game save tampering the 
  programmers made it harder to transfer saves from one machine to another. 
  The only preferred method for transferring saves is to move them into PSN's 
  cloud server then onto the new machine.

  If you used other devices, such as an SD Card, then you may run into the 
  "You did not create this game save" problem which will cause you not to be 
  able to use that save even though all you are doing is moving them to 
  another machine. According to a friend of mine this is related to 
  unformatted devices.

  If the device is not formatted by the PS3 then any GTA V save from it will 
  not be recognized and cannot be used. The reason for that is GTA V is 
  programmed in such a way is that if the save device is not PS3 formatted 
  then it is assumed to be a third party device and further to be assumed to 
  be a cheat device thus the restriction on saves.

  If the device is PS3 formatted then you should have no problem transferring 
  saves from one machine to another.

  Unfortunately, it is not as easy as you think to PS3 format devices. The 
  only way to properly format save devices is through the built-in media 
  slots on the old original PS3 "Fatty" units. You cannot format devices 
  through the USB slot even if you attach a multi-card reader to it. 
  Fortunately there are programs out on the net that will allow you to resign 
  saves so you can use them again on a new machine.

  The majority of games will allow you to move saves between machines using 
  standard Windows formatted devices. Only a handful of games, such as in the 
  case of GTA V, restrict movement of saves.

| A. On Foot |~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~\
0+=+=+=+=+=+=0=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+0

As with any GTA game, there are plenty of things you can do when on foot.

0===========================================================================0
|           Command          |       Xbox 360       |     PlayStation 3     |
0===========================================================================0
| Move Around................|    Left Analog Stick |     Left Analog Stick |
| Rotate Camera..............|   Right Analog Stick |    Right Analog Stick |
| Sneak Mode.................|    Left Stick Button |             L3 Button |
| Look Behind/Zoom Aim.......|   Right Stick Button |             R3 Button |
| [1] Multiple Use...........|             A Button |              X Button |
| [2] Multiple Use...........|             X Button |         Square Button |
| [3] Multiple Use...........|             B Button |         Circle Button |
| Enter Vehicle..............|             Y Button |       Triangle Button |
| Target.....................|         Left Trigger |             L2 Button |
| Fire Weapon/Melee Attack...|        Right Trigger |             R2 Button |
| [4] Weapon Wheel...........|          Left Bumper |             L1 Button |
| Enter/Exit Cover...........|         Right Bumper |             R1 Button |
| Use Cell Phone.............|             D-Pad Up |              D-Pad Up |
| [5] Character Wheel........|           D-Pad Down |            D-Pad Down |
| Detonate Sticky Bomb.......|           D-Pad Left |            D-Pad Left |
| [6] Multiple Use...........|          D-Pad Right |           D-Pad Right |
| Change Camera Mode.........|          Back Button |         Select Button |
| Pause......................|         Start Button |          Start Button |
0===========================================================================0

[1] - This button is used for different actions:
        --Run (hold down).
        --Sprint (tap).
        --Going up and down ladders faster.
        --Cell Phone (used to answer calls).
        --Various mission specific actions.

[2] - This button is used for different actions:
        --Jump (when running).
        --Climb (when running at a short wall).
        --Various mission specific actions.

[3] - This button is used for different actions:
        --Reload Weapon.
        --Cell Phone (ignoring calls and hanging up).
        --Melee Fighting (punching, swinging, stabbing, and countering).
        --Various mission specific actions.

[4] - Hold down to bring up the Wheel, tap to bring out or holster selected 
      weapon.

[5] - This can also be used to bring up your character's Stats.

[6] - This is used for different actions:
        --Talk to a ped or Cop.
        --Interact with certain objects.
        --Hail a Cab.

| B. In Cars, Motorcycles, Boats, and Sub |~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~\
0+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+0+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+0

As with all the other GTAs, there are plenty of vehicles to use in GTA V.
From cars and motorcycles to speedboats. They can all be used here. When
driving a vehicle there are some things to note.

First, if you smash into something hard enough, you may go flying out of the
windshield of a car.

Second, if you fling yourself out of a car or off a motorcycle at a high rate
of speed, you will seriously hurt yourself. The faster you go, the more
damage you will suffer.

And, finally, you can shoot 360 degrees from a vehicle (good for slowing down
Police pursuit) and you can use multiple weapons while driving.

|           Command          |       Xbox 360       |     PlayStation 3     |
0===========================================================================0

| Rotate Camera/Aim..........|   Right Analog Stick |    Right Analog Stick |
| [1] Horn...................|    Left Stick Button |     Left Stick Button |
| Look Behind................|   Right Stick Button |    Right Stick Button |
| [2] Multiple Use...........|             A Button |              X Button |
| [3] Switch Weapons.........|             X Button |         Square Button |
| [4] Cinematic Camera.......|             B Button |         Circle Button |
| Enter/Exit Vehicle.........|             Y Button |       Triangle Button |
| Brake/Reverse..............|         Left Trigger |             L2 Button |
| Accelerate.................|        Right Trigger |             R2 Button |

            /=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=\
 /=========================================================================\
| >GEN5. Other Modes of Transportation                                      |
 \=========================================================================/
            \=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=/

In addition to the above vehicles you can control, there are two modes of
alternate transportation you can use to get around Los Santos:

0======0
| Train \
0====================================================>

  Los Santos has an extensive train system that runs under the north, 
  southeast, and airport areas. All you have to do to use the train is to 
  enter one when it stops at a station. You'll automatically sit down when 
  the train starts then get up again when it stops. Then you can walk out 
  when you feel you are close to your destination.

0=====0
| Taxi \
0====================================================>

  Another mode of alternate transportation is the Taxi Cab. Use D-Pad Right 
  to hail when you close to one on foot and tap the Enter Vehicle button to 
  enter as a passenger. You can then select from various destinations but 
  only the ones that have an icon on the map. You can select to hurry the 
  ride, skip to the end, or simply enjoy the experience.

            /=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=\
 /=========================================================================\
| >GEN7. The Three Protagonists                                             |
 \=========================================================================/
            \=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=/

Although GTA V has a bunch of new and interesting features the biggest one by
far is the fact that you control three people instead of one. This makes for
an interesting and intriguing gaming experience. When you unlock the other
characters then hold Down on the D-Pad to bring up the Character Wheel which
will appear at the lower right corner of the screen. Then use the Right
Analog Stick to select your character.

You will then zoom out into the sky away from the previous character and zoom
in on the new one. As you finish zooming in you may find your selected
character in the middle of some activity, sometimes humorous.

Each of the three characters has a color designation that gives you an
indication of what missions and activities are available to him:

  --Franklin (green)
  --Michael (blue)
  --Trevor (orange)

When you bring up the Character Wheel you may see a number attached to each
person. This indicates how many open missions are available to him. It is
also important to note that you cannot switch characters when you have a
Wanted Rating.

Another thing to note about the three men - each has a different sleep rate.
This means that when you make a character sleep the rate of time passage is
different for each one: Franklin (eight hours), Michael (six hours), Trevor
(twelve hours).

Finally, each character has his own personal car which can always be found at
his Safehouse. Franklin has the Buffalo, Michael has the Tailgater, and
Trevor has the Bodhi. You can wreck or lose the car somewhere and go back to
your Safehouse to get another one. It is highly recommended that you mod your
car as soon as possible to improve its speed and handling which will be
useful on many missions.

            /=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=\
 /=========================================================================\
| >GEN8. The Main Screen                                                    |
 \=========================================================================/
            \=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=/

Your Main Screen is where all of the action in GTA V takes place.

In the center of your screen is your selected character (Franklin, Michael,
Trevor). You use your Left Analog Stick to move him around and the Right
Analog Stick to rotate and manipulate the camera when he is standing still.

In the lower left corner of the Main Screen is the Radar. This is used to
help in finding your current position in the city, objectives, mission
strands, Safehouses, and other areas.

There is also a line, broken into three segments, that is under the Radar.
This line represents the following:

0===========================================================================0
| Health          | The green portion of this line is the longest. When it  |
|                 | is gone then you will be Wasted. However, when it is    |
|                 | down under 50%, then it will regenerate up to 50%.      |
|                 |                                                         |
|                 | You have to be standing still in order for this to      |
|                 | happen. You can improve your ability to sustain damage  |
|                 | by increasing your Strength Skill (covered later).      |
|-----------------+---------------------------------------------------------|
| Armor           | The blue portion of this line represents the amount of  |
|                 | Body Armor you have. When it is gone then you will      |
|                 | start losing Health when you take damage.               |
|-----------------+---------------------------------------------------------|
| Special Ability | The yellow portion of this line represents how much you |
|                 | can use your Special Ability. Each character has a      |
|                 | special talent that requires certain actions to fill up |
|                 | this portion of the line.                               |
0===========================================================================0

In the upper right corner of the Main Screen you will find the amount of
money you have (and your Wanted Rating if any). However, most of the time
there will be nothing in the upper right corner. You have to press D-Pad Down
or come back from a paused game to get the info to appear.

Special prompts will appear at either the upper left corner of the Main
Screen or at the bottom. When you open your Cell Phone it will appear in the
lower right part of the screen.

       <0+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+<<##0##>>+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+0>

There are also some interesting tricks that can quickly increase certain
Skills:

0==================================0
| Raising Special Abilities Quickly \
0=========================================================>

  Each character has a different Special Ability. It was thought that you had 
  to do certain things while using the Ability in order to increase it. But, 
  according to GameFAQs user shadowlucas27, he found that what actually 
  raises the Skill is filling the Special Ability meter - not by using it.

  Although both Michael and Trevor have combat based Special Abilities all of 
  them have one method in common to fill up the Special Bar - driving fast in 
  vehicles.

  So, the safest way to max out your Special is by getting a fast car and 
  driving down the major highways real fast. In addition to driving fast, 
  passing cars very closely gives a significant boost to the meter.

  Once it is filled up then you need to drain it so you can fill it up again 
  and raise your Special. Franklin's Ability is vehicle related so he can 
  drain and refill his meter very quickly which will rapidly raise his 
  Special.

  But both Michael and Trevor can't use their Special while in a car so, 
  after filling up the meter, pull off to the side of the road, get out, and 
  activate the Special to drain the meter. Then get back in your car and 
  quickly drive down the road to refill the meter then pull off again to 
  drain it. Repeat until your Special is maxed out. This probably takes less 
  than ten minutes per character.

  It is important to note that for Trevor you won't see a gradual increase of 
  his Special. It will appear to not be advancing even after a couple of 
  refills. Be assured, though, that you are indeed increasing the Special, 
  it's just that it advances in jumps. When you get to a certain level then 
  it will jump to that.

  It is also very important to note that for Michael you can't increase his 
  Special until after the mission "Father/Son".

0=======================0
| The Bus Stomping Trick \
0=========================================================>

  One trick that has been floating around various forums is to stomp a bus to 
  quickly increase your Strength. The transit buses that roam the city have 
  people inside of them. If you climb the bus to the top and attack you will 
  stomp the bus instead of just swinging into thin air.

  The game actually thinks you are attacking the people on the bus but the 
  roof keeps you from hitting them. But it still counts as a melee attack 
  thus allowing you to increase your Strength.

  However, as you attack, the bus driver will become spooked and drive fast 
  along his route. In addition, you will risk the Police being called to come 
  after you as well as falling off the bus.

  But you can simply jack the bus, take it to a reasonably secluded area, 
  park it near something you can climb (so you can get on top of the bus), 
  then stomp the bus to your heart's content without falling off or 
  generating Wanted Ratings. The people will stay inside the bus.

  It is important to note that not all buses have people in them. Make sure 
  that there are people inside before jacking the bus. Although you can stomp 
  an empty bus you will not be able to increase your Strength because there 
  is nobody inside.

0================================0
| The System Hardware Pause Trick \
0=========================================================>

  A GameFAQs user named bookeworm came up with this interesting trick which 
  involves the use of the System Hardware Pause.

  There are two types of pause within a game - the pause menu within the game 
  and the system hardware pause. The system hardware pause is activated by 
  either using the Guide Button (Xbox 360) or PS Button (PS3) that can be 
  found in the center of their respective joypads.

  The trick involves using the system hardware pause to pause the game while 
  doing a specific action related to one of the Skills and let the game 
  increase it while you do something else.

  For example, start running then press the System Hardware Button to pause 
  the game. For some reason, even though the game is paused this way, the 
  game thinks you are still running. Thus you can still increase your Stamina 
  Skill even though the game is paused.

  Go do something else for awhile then come back and un-pause the game. You 
  will see that your Stamina has greatly increased even though your character 
  hadn't moved an inch. This trick works with Stamina, Stealth, Flying, and 
  Driving Skills.

  For the Driving Skill you need to do a wheelie on a motorcycle as this will 
  not work when just driving down the street. To easily pop a wheelie, hold 
  down the Handbrake Button while holding down the Accelerate Button. This 
  will cause the engine to rev up.

  Pull back on the Left Analog Stick then release the Handbrake Button. This 
  will cause you to wheelie and immediately hit the System Hardware Button 
  while you are in this position.

            /=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=\
 /=========================================================================\
| >GEN10. The Map                                                           |
 \=========================================================================/
            \=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=/

Pausing the game will automatically bring up the in-game map of the entire
area. However, unlike the other GTA installments, the map is only partially
exposed. Only the immediate areas surrounding you and the various places of
interest, such as Ammu-Nations and Safehouses, are seen.

To expose the entire map you have to explore the entire area. The fastest way
is by using either a plane or helicopter. There is even an Accomplishment for
exposing the map.

When using the map you can set waypoints for your GPS. Given the size of the
map you will be using this often as you go from area to area. You can even
set points of interest so you can return to a particular spot later.

            /=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=\
 /=========================================================================\
| >GEN11. Quick Saving                                                      |
 \=========================================================================/
            \=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=/

One of the handy features of this game is the ability to save anywhere and at
any time. Given that you have one Safehouse to a character this is a
necessity. Bring up your Cell Phone and there will be the cloud icon on the
left side. From here you can save your game in progress.

One neat thing about Quick Save is that it can repair cars. If you save while
in a car that has been seriously damaged then reload that save you will find
that the car has been fully repaired.

But you need to be careful when saving. If you save while you have a Wanted
Rating then you will still have it when you reload the save. The Wanted
Rating does not go away in the same manner that it does when you save at a
Safehouse.

            /=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=\
 /=========================================================================\
| >GEN12. Animals                                                           |
 \=========================================================================/
            \=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=/

One of the new features in GTA V is animals. Well, to be technical there have
been animals in the GTA games before but they were mainly birds (and the
human kind). But now there are several more types of animals including deer,
coyotes, cows, and fish in addition to birds. These animals are harmless and
will either fly, run, or swim away when you get close.

But not all animals are passive. There are some that will attack you if they
appear near you. You can tell that one is near when you see a red dot on your
radar. And these animals are:

0===========================================================================0
| Dogs    | For the most part the dogs in this game are passive and will do |
|         | no harm. But if you attack someone near a dog then that animal  |
|         | will most likely attack you.                                    |
|---------+-----------------------------------------------------------------|
| Cougars | These animals can be found in the mountain areas and were a     |
|         | pain in the ass in "Red Dead Redemption".                       |
|         |                                                                 |
|         | However, in GTA V, you have automobiles that you can use to run |
|         | these furry little shits down when you see them on the side of  |
|         | the road. On foot they can very quickly kill you if they manage |
|         | to get the jump on you but superior firepower will put these    |
|         | bad little kitties in a bad little place with little effort.    |
|---------+-----------------------------------------------------------------|
| Sharks  | You can find these guys way out into the ocean. As long as you  |
|         | keep your distance and don't do anything stupid they might not  |
|         | do anything. When they attack though, one bite is fatal. There  |
|         | is even an Accomplishment for getting attacked by a Shark.      |
0===========================================================================0

At some point early in the game you will even be given a pet dog named Chop
that you can use for various activities or to play with to pass the time.

            /=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=\
 /=========================================================================\
| >GEN14. Melee Fighting and Hostiles                                       |
 \=========================================================================/
            \=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=/

In past installments melee fighting with peds was almost considered an
afterthought. There was a slight improvement in GTA IV but has been greatly
improved in GTA V and made more fun. Although you only use one button for
throwing punches and kicks your character seems to throw the right punch at
the right moment even if a ped is coming from behind. The way peds react when
you hit them makes this a lot of fun.

And it is even more fun when you use Baseball Bats, Crowbars, and even
pistolwhipping people in the face.

But melee fighting people, or even just knocking them down when simply
running past them, may make other peds nearby hostile showing up on the radar
as red dots. More often than not they will fight you with their fists.
However, if you are in the wrong part of town, such as Grove St., then you
will find yourself in a very nasty firefight with pretty much the entire
neighborhood.

If you are trespassing in certain areas after dark, such as construction
sites, then you may end up facing the patrolling security guards who will
more often or not shoot at you.

And while we're on the subject of firefights.....

            /=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=\
 /=========================================================================\
| >GEN15. Firearm and Weapon Usage                                          |
 \=========================================================================/
            \=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=/

Firearm usage is not much different from GTA IV's. When you are on foot and
hold down the Target Button then you will go into an over-the-shoulder view.
The aiming reticle will be a simple white dot but you can change its size
from Simple to Complex in the Settings tab at the Pause Screen.

Press the Right Analog Stick Button to activate the weapon's zoom feature.
When you move the reticle over a person then you can intimidate or frighten
that person. You can also aim at specific parts of a person. You can shoot a
person in the arm, shoulder, leg, midsection, and head.

You can score a one-hit kill with a headshot. You can also shoot a person in
any other part and they will run away when they get up. Whenever a person
dies, regardless of how you kill them, the screen will briefly flash white to
let you know.

There are three aiming styles that can help you get the most out of combat
situations:

0===========================================================================0
| GTA Traditional | This will allow you to quickly lock onto the nearest    |
|                 | target regardless of where he is, even if he is behind  |
|                 | you. It will also "hard lock" onto the chest.           |
|                 |                                                         |
|                 | What this means is that if you try to move the reticle  |
|                 | away from the chest it will try to stay there meaning   |
|                 | that it will be difficult to hit other body parts like  |
|                 | the leg or head.                                        |
|-----------------+---------------------------------------------------------|
| Assisted Aiming | This will allow you to quickly lock onto the nearest    |
|                 | target within a certain radius in front of you even if  |
|                 | the closest target is actually behind you.              |
|                 |                                                         |
|                 | This mode also has a "soft lock". It will aim at the    |
|                 | chest but you can move the reticle to any part of the   |
|                 | target's body without resistance.                       |
|                 |                                                         |
|                 | This is the aiming style that you should use throughout |
|                 | the game as it will make combat, in and out of          |
|                 | missions, easier.                                       |
|-----------------+---------------------------------------------------------|
| Free Aim        | There is no lock whatsoever. You can only aim in front  |
|                 | of you. This is recommended for experts or those        |
|                 | looking for a challenge.                                |
0===========================================================================0

When you are in a car and press the Left Bumper (Xbox 360) or L1 Button (PS3)
then you will break out the window of your car and the reticle will appear as
you start firing. Use the Right Analog Stick to aim the reticle. 

You can use your Pistols, the Micro SMG, and the majority of your thrown
explosive weapons. When on a motorcycle you can also use the Sawed-Off
Shotgun. When unarmed you can give passers-by the finger and make rude
remarks. In addition, your weapon choices may be limited depending on what
vehicle you use.

Of course, when you start attacking the innocent and not-so-innocent
population of Blaine County and Los Santos, then you will attract the
attention of.....

            /=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=\
 /=========================================================================\
| >GEN16. Law Enforcement                                                   |
 \=========================================================================/
            \=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=/

Every metropolis has a Police force and Los Santos is no different. When you
do something bad near a Cop, or someone calls 911 on you (yes, pedestrians
will do that sometimes - even if you're just standing in front of them), then
you will attract Police attention and they will try to bust you.

One of the biggest criticisms, if not the biggest, of GTA V is the Police. In
this installment they are much more aggressive, more accurate with their
firearms, and much tougher to kill. The main focus in dealing with them is to
avoid confrontations by giving you better means of getting away from them.

However, they are also known for magically appearing all around you, even on
mountain tops, and finding you regardless of where you may happen to be
hiding and this has furthered this particular criticism.

Another interesting difference from previous installments - there is no
6-Star Wanted Rating. The maximum for this game is five. I don't quite
understand the change as 6-Stars was the traditional Wanted Rating maximum
from the beginning of the entire series.

0+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=0=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+0
| A. When You Are Wanted |~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~\
0+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=0=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+0

When you get a Wanted Rating you will see the Radar flash red. However, you
won't see any Police on there. You are given some time to leave the area
before the Cops show up. When they do show up they will go to where the crime
was committed. You will also see a cone on each Police dot. This is their
line of sight. Your goal is to avoid their lines of sight as you flee the
scene.

While you are out of sight then you will see your Wanted Rating flash in the
upper right corner. You are in what is called the cooldown period. Over time
the Wanted Rating will flash slower and slower until it stops. When it stops
then the Wanted Rating disappears and the Police will stop pursuit.

If the Police spot you or you commit another crime during the cooldown period
then you will be re-acquired and you must lose the Police all over again.

To get away from them you should go through narrow hidden alleys and tunnels.
As noted, this is not always a guarantee of losing them as they seem to know
where you are hiding so keep moving when they start to creep on you.

If you get a Rating on foot and either break into a nearby car or go into a
large bush then you may see your marker go dark on the radar. This indicates
that you are hidden from the Police. This will make it harder for them to
find you. But, if they get too close to you, then they will see you and you
will be re-acquired.

As noted, the Police also have a habit of magically appearing in front of you
while you are trying to flee from them. Usually when this happens they will
have their back to you. In this instance you don't want to go too fast as
this will give you time to alter your course before he turns around and finds
you.

It should be pointed out that Cops can and will take civilian vehicles to
pursue you.

0+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=0=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+0
| B. Getting Rid of Wanted Ratings |~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~\
0+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=0=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+0

In addition of escaping from them, using a Los Santos Customs or getting
Busted, other methods of getting rid of a Wanted Rating include getting
Wasted and saving your game at your Safehouse.

What's interesting is that you don't even have to save the game in a save
slot. Just get to the save screen and then back out. Your Wanted Ratings, no
matter how high, are gone (plus you advance time about six to twelve hours
depending on your character).

0+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+0+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+0
| C. The Wanted Ratings |~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~\
0+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+0+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+0

There are five Wanted Rating levels. The higher you go, the more aggressive
the pursuit. Below are the Wanted Ratings and what you can expect:

0=======0
| 1-Star \
0=====================================>

  The Cops will draw their weapons and come up to you in an attempt to arrest 
  you. If they get close enough then you will be arrested.

0=======0
| 2-Star \
0=====================================>

  If you run away from a Cop when he is close enough to arrest you or shoot 
  near a Cop without hitting him then your Wanted Rating will go up to 
  2-Star. At this point more Cops will join in the chase and they will start 
  shooting at you.

  When in vehicles they will start ramming into the rear of your car in an 
  attempt to veer you off the road. They will also try to get in front of you 
  to block your way and trap you between Police cars in an attempt to stop 
  you.

0=======0
| 3-Star \
0=====================================>

  If you shoot at and hit a Cop or physically assault (either melee or 
  vehicle) one then your Wanted Rating automatically goes up to 3-Star. At 
  this point more Police vehicles will get involved. When you wound a Cop he 
  may try to shoot you from the ground.

  The Police will also send out a Police Maverick. The Police Maverick has 
  two heavily armored SWAT wielding Carbine Rifles and will shoot down at you 
  (and quite accurately I might add). You can chase the Police Maverick away 
  by killing the gunmen on the chopper. A well placed shot to the head of the 
  pilot will bring down the chopper. Also shooting up the tail rotor a few 
  times will destroy it and crash the helicopter.

  The helicopter also has a wide and large angle of view which will make it 
  much harder to get rid of Wanted Ratings. The best way generally to get out 
  of their sight is to go into tunnels. But the chopper may fly away during 
  pursuit for refueling which will make it easier to evade the Police.

  If you try to escape by water then you will be chased by Police Predator
  boats (which seem to magically appear out of nowhere and close to you).

  These boats will carry at least one Cop, wielding a Micro SMG, at the back 
  of the boat. Considering that you are very vulnerable when swimming, these 
  Predators will shred you very quickly if you stay in the water for too 
  long. Although, if you are in the right boat, then you can easily outrun 
  them.

  They will also start to blockade the road in an attempt to stop you. At 
  this point you may start to see the Police Transporter vehicle. It is 
  usually manned by one Cop and there will be a tire busting spike strip in 
  front of it.

  You will also note that if you aren't playing music from the radio then you 
  will start to hear music that plays when you are being chased by the 
  Police. This music will end when the chase ends either by successfully 
  evading them, getting Busted, or getting Wasted.

0=======0
| 4-Star \
0=====================================>

  More vehicles will get involved in the pursuit and the roadblocks get 
  tougher to breach. The Cops will start wearing bulletproof vests which will 
  make them harder to kill. You may also start to see the Police Riot vehicle 
  in the blockades.

  A second Police Maverick will now be added to the pursuit. In addition, the 
  choppers will also start to rappel SWAT down towards your position (though 
  they can be easily shot down as they drop).

  In addition, the Federal Investigation Bureau (FIB) gets involved. They 
  drive up in the FIB sport utility vehicle which will also have two SWAT 
  gunmen hanging off the sides. Although vulnerable they are also very 
  accurate with their Pistols and will kill you quickly if you hang around 
  them too long. The driver will also shoot at you - something the other Cops 
  don't do.

  If you enter Fort Zancudo you will get an automatic 4-Star Wanted Rating 
  and you will have to deal with the Army which don't take kindly to 
  trespassers. They tend to drive around in jeeps and tanks. The tanks, 
  covered in a little bit, will kill you with one shot of their powerful 
  cannons.

0=======0
| 5-Star \
0=====================================>

  There will be no new vehicle types added to the pursuit but there will be 
  more Police chasing you in the last valiant attempt to take you down.

0+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+0+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+0

become less sensitive so you can go exploring certain areas or to do general

  >>Fair Game (Cletus)

| F. Busted |~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~\
0+=+=+=+=+=+0+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+0

If the Cops end up catching you, be it on foot or in a vehicle, then you are
Busted. Any mission you were doing at the time will be Failed. When you are
Busted you are sent to the nearest Police Station where you will be processed
(which takes six game hours) and released.

In previous installments you would lose all of your weapons when Busted. In
GTA V you get to keep your weapons but the Cops will take your ammo instead.
It will also cost you $300 in bail money upon release.

There are nine Police Stations in Blaine County and Los Santos where you may
find yourself if you are Busted by the Cops:

| G. Police Vehicles |~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~\
0+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=0=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+0

In addition to all of the other cars you can drive in GTA V you can also use
Police Vehicles. Some Police Vehicles have additional features and bonuses

  >>Police Cruiser
    **************
      Found: On the street and at most Police Stations in Los Santos.

| H. Special Vehicles |~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~\
0+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+0+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+0

There are three special Police and Army vehicles of note:

  >>Buzzard Attack Chopper
    **********************
      This helicopter can sometimes be found on top of the N.O.O.S.E. 
      building and at Fort Zancudo. This aircraft carries both Rockets and 
      Machine Guns and can be switched with the Switch Weapons Button.

      Although this sounds like a cool chopper to use for general chaos it is 
      hard to aim at anything on the ground because of the constant swaying 
      of the chopper regardless of your Flying Skill. Even more interesting 
      is the fact that the Rockets won't lock onto anything other than Police 
      vehicles.

  >>Rhino Tank
    **********
      This vehicle can only be found at Fort Zancudo and is one of the 
      tougher vehicles of the game. The Tank Cannon is controlled by the 
      Right Analog Stick and the lower body is controlled by the Left Analog 
      Stick. The cannon itself is very powerful and can easily blow up 
      multiple vehicles at once. The cannon can angle high enough to shoot 
      down low flying helicopters.

      Even though the tank looks tough it can still be destroyed. Gunfire 
      will gradually, but slowly, damage the vehicle. Vehicle collisions, 
      especially if the cars you're running over explode, can seriously and 
      quickly damage the tank. A handful of explosive collisions will be 
      enough to destroy the tank.

      Acquiring a tank from the base can be a chore because of the 4-Star 
      Wanted Rating which can often result in getting killed before you can 
      drive away with your prize. But a GameFAQs user, Korben_Dallas_5, came 
      up with this easy way to acquire the Rhino with minimum fuss.

      Go into the hills just north of the base and overlooking the sewage 
      treatment plant. Use a Sniper Rifle and aim at one of the patrolling 
      tanks inside the base. Fire one shot at it and you will get a 2-Star 
      Wanted Rating. At this point the tanks will leave the base and head to 
      your position.

      Stay high up and out of their view or they will start shooting their 
      cannons at you. At least one of them will enter the plant and roam 
      below you. When the Rating is gone then quickly climb down and jack the 
      tank before it can leave the area. This will result in another 2-Star 
      Wanted Rating but it will be easier to lose this as opposed to a 
      4-Star.

      Try to head to the beach to the west without running over any vehicles 
      as this is the best bet to lose the Rating. After you lose it then take 
      your new toy to anyplace that will store it.

  >>P-996 Lazer
    ***********
      This plane can only be found at Fort Zancudo. This is a fighter jet 
      that has both Cannons and Missiles. However, you are moving too fast 
      for this to be of much use. Most people tend to use this plane for the 
      Knife Flights or to challenge themselves to see if they can get the 
      plane out of the base without being shot down by the hostile Army.

0+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=0=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+0
| I. Impound Lot |~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~\
0+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=0=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+0

If you're driving a car that is not your personal vehicle then you run the
risk of it being impounded by the Cops. The vehicle will be kept at the
Impound Lot at the Mission Row Police Station. It will cost $200 to get the
vehicle out. The Cops can only impound one car at a time so once they take a
car then you don't have to worry about them taking another one unless you get
the first one out.

            /=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=\
 /=========================================================================\
| >GEN17. Vehicle and Aircraft Damage                                       |
 \=========================================================================/
            \=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=/

The cars in GTA V are much tougher than those in GTA IV. They have to be
really because of the Police. If the damage parameters were the same as GTA
IV then the Police will be able to easily destroy your car before you got
more than a few feet. So the cars are made to be more like tanks in regards
to firearm damage.

The weakest point of a car is the engine. But it will still take considerable
damage to get it to flame. You can slow down the car by blowing out the tires
and/or ruining the alignment which will cause one of the front wheels to lock
up. Alignment damage can vary from vehicle to vehicle.

Sometimes, if you shoot or wreck the car from underneath, you may see liquid
pour out from the car. In this case you have punctured the gas tank and the
fuel is spilling out onto the road. You can easily blow up the car if you
fire into the trail which will light up the gas tank. Of course, if you're
driving said car, you will be Wasted. But, even if the gas isn't lit up, the
car will eventually stop as the fuel runs out.

Aircraft are even more fragile. Even taking a few minor rounds or simply
scraping on a building anywhere on the craft will eventually lead to it
stalling out in midair as it "bleeds out". This can be frustrating if you are
just trying to get the hang of flying around in a stolen plane or chopper.

            /=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=\
 /=========================================================================\
| >GEN18. Using a Los Santos Customs                                        |
 \=========================================================================/
            \=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=/

As noted earlier, you can drive a car, excluding Police and rescue vehicles,
into a Los Santos Customs to get rid of Wanted Ratings. In order to get rid
of Wanted Ratings you *MUST* be out of sight of the Cops otherwise you can't
use this service. When they finish up the vehicle then the Wanted Ratings
will be gone.

However, in this GTA installment, they can do a lot more than get rid of
Wanted Ratings and repair your vehicle. You can use them to modify your
vehicle in a large variety of ways including adding armor and changing things
from color all the way to transmissions.

Each listing of modification has several levels with each one being more
extensive and expensive. But not all levels are available at the start and
will unlock progressively during the course of the game. With these services
you can really trick out your car into something that will make the people
you pass by very jealous.

There are five Los Santos Customs and other garages in Blaine County and Los
Santos where you can use these services:

  >>Beeker's Garage
    ***************
      Where: Paleto Bay, Blaine County (on Procopio Dr.).
      Map: (B-4).

  >>Los Santos Customs
    ******************
      Where: Grand Senora Desert, Blaine County (on Route 68).
      Map: (D-5).

  >>Los Santos Customs
    ******************
      Where: Burton, Los Santos (near Hawick Avenue).
      Map: (G-4).

  >>Los Santos Customs
    ******************
      Where: La Mesa, Los Santos (near Popular St.).
      Map: (G-5).

  >>Los Santos Customs
    ******************
      Where: Los Santos International Airport, Los Santos (on Greenwich 
             Parkway).
      Map: (H-3).

 /=========================================================================\
| >GEN19. Wasted                                                            |
 \=========================================================================/
            \=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=/

If you do something to reduce your Health to zero, like being too close to an
explosion, getting shot up a lot, wiping out big time on a motorcycle, or
getting eaten by a Shark then you will be Wasted. Any mission you were doing
at the time will be Failed.

When you are Wasted then you are sent to the nearest Hospital where you will
be treated (which takes six game hours), billed percentage of whatever amount
of money you have (up to $5,000), and released. You also lose your Body Armor
but you will *NOT* lose your weapons or ammo.

There are five Hospitals in Blaine County and Los Santos where you may find
yourself if you are Wasted for any reason:

  >>Paleto Bay Care Center

      Map: (B-4).

      Map: (D-5).

  >>Mount Zonah Medical Center
    **************************
      Region: Rockford Hills, Los Santos.
      Location: Along Dorset Drive.
      Map: (G-4).

  >>Pillbox Hill Medical Center
    ***************************

  >>Central Los Santos Medical Center
    *********************************

            /=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=\
 /=========================================================================\
| >GEN20. 100% Score                                                        |
 \=========================================================================/
            \=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=/

A feature that was introduced in "The Ballad of Gay Tony" was the 100% Score,
one that returns with this installment. Usually the main goal is to get
through the mission without failing. But there are other goals, such as
mission time, player and car damage, to keep track of as well.

It is important to note that getting 100% Score in each mission is *NOT*
required for 100% Completion. You can play through the game just like all of
the other installments and completely ignore this if you like. One change
from TBoGT is that you will get a Medal for the mission and what type of
Medal you get is determined by your score.

If you finish a mission without completing any of the optional Requirements
you will get a Bronze Medal. If you complete the mission with some or most of
the Requirements you will get a Silver Medal. If you complete the mission
with all of the Requirements completed then you will get a Gold Medal. There
is an Accomplishment for acquiring Gold Medals for most of the missions and
encounters.

Another important thing to note about the 100% Score is that you do *NOT*
have to do all of the Requirements at one time. You can do most of them
during your initial play-through of a mission then redo it later, through the
Replay Mission or Replay Strangers and Freaks in the Game tab, to get what
you missed. Unlike with TBoGT you do not have to wait until the end of the
game before doing Mission Replays - you can do them at any time.

What this means is that you can play the same mission over but focus on a
particular Requirement, such as Time, for example. Once you get that
Requirement then you don't have to worry about that again. Then you can play
the mission again and focus on another Requirement.

Continue going after each Requirement in successive play-throughs until you
have 100% Score in that mission. This accumulative approach makes things
easier and also makes you play through these missions in different ways.

It is important to note, though, that when you replay a mission you will only
have a very small amount of money to use and that whatever health, armor, and
ammo you have before starting the replay will carry over. If you don't have
full health and armor then you may want to fix that before replaying.

Another thing to note is that on some missions you will be placed in another
position different than the one you started on in the initial play-through.
Certain vehicles and items may also be changed in a replay.

You can also use powerful weapons, and their various modifications, that you
will acquire during the course of the game in replays of missions that occur
early in the game. One option to consider is to play all the way through to
the end of the Main Story without replaying any of the missions then use your
new weaponry on the missions you wish to replay. This may make getting some
of the Requirements much easier.

If you fail a mission then certain Requirements will be nullified if you want
to replay from the point of failure. If you have trouble with part of a
mission then you can skip it to move it forward so you can complete it.
However, if you do that, then *ALL* Requirements for that mission will be
nullified.

There are some Requirements that are common to many missions:

0===========================================================================0
| Time      | For this you need to complete the mission within a time       |
|           | limit. It goes without saying that you need to get to your    |
|           | destinations, kill everyone in your way, and complete all     |
|           | objectives as quickly as possible. However, whenever needed,  |
|           | I will go over shortcuts that can be very useful.             |
|           |                                                               |
|           | If you fail the mission then this will be nullified. If you   |
|           | want the Requirement then you will have to back out of the    |
|           | Replay and completely redo it from scratch.                   |
|-----------+---------------------------------------------------------------|
| Accuracy  | For this you need to complete the mission above a certain     |
|           | amount of shots hit. Going for body shots will increase the   |
|           | number of shots hit which will help your percentage. Like     |
|           | with the Time Requirement, if you fail the mission then it    |
|           | will be nullified.                                            |
|-----------+---------------------------------------------------------------|
| Headshots | For this you need to complete the mission with a certain      |
|           | number of headshots. Pretty straightforward and can be made   |
|           | easier by using certain weapons which I will go over in just  |
|           | a bit.                                                        |
|-----------+---------------------------------------------------------------|
| Unmarked  | For this you need to complete the mission with minimal damage |
|           | to health and armor. Take your time and use your cover        |
|           | wisely. However, even if you lose health you can still get    |
|           | this by refilling it before the mission ends.                 |
|           |                                                               |
|           | But I believe you can only refill it once - if you refill a   |
|           | second time then you may not get the Requirement. Failing the |
|           | mission will also nullify it.                                 |
0===========================================================================0

There are couple of things that can make a big difference in some of the
above Requirements:

0===========================================================================0
| Aiming Style | Using Assisted Aiming will be a very big help as it will   |
|              | allow you to very quickly target and kill enemies with a   |
|              | high degree of accuracy. I don't recommend using GTA       |
|              | Traditional as it is too much of a hard lock and will make |
|              | it harder to aim at certain body parts like the head.      |
|--------------+------------------------------------------------------------|
| Weapons      | Certain weapons can also make a big difference. Perhaps    |
|              | one of the best weapons I found for the Time, Accuracy,    |
|              | and Headshot Requirements is the use of the Assault        |
|              | Shotgun. It has a wide spread which lessens the need for   |
|              | accurate aiming and kills quickly resulting in fewer shots |
|              | fired.                                                     |
|              |                                                            |
|              | For targets farther away I recommend the use of either the |
|              | Carbine Rifle, Advanced Rifle, or the Combat MG.           |
0===========================================================================0

            /=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=\
 /=========================================================================\
| >GEN21. The Stock Market                                                  |
 \=========================================================================/
            \=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=/

One of the interesting features of this game is the stock markets where you
can make lots of money. To find it you bring up your phone and go into the
Internet. Go into Money and Services and you should find the two exchanges -
LCN Exchange and BAWSAQ. LCN Exchange has about half of the companies found
in the game while BAWSAQ has the other half.

One important thing to note is that BAWSAQ can only used online - you need to
be connected to the real internet in order to use it. LCN Exchange is the
offline market.

There are plenty of companies to choose from. Each company has basic
information on it and a general idea of how it is currently trending.
However, the graphs used for each company is useless and should not be used
to make a decision on investment.

Just like with the real stock market the prices of all stock seem to move up
and down randomly. But certain missions can help boost or drop certain stock
which you can take advantage of to make lots of money. There are only a
handful of missions, most notably the Lester Assassination missions, that
will manipulate certain stocks to your advantage.

When using these missions you should get all three characters to invest all
of their money in certain stocks before the mission or after the mission is
completed. You may also have to wait several game days for these stocks to
either drop or max out. For this you should sleep at your Safehouse until the
stocks are right where you want them.

It is very important to note that doing things off-mission cannot make the
market change. Attacking one business to make its stock drop will not work.
If it did then it would be way too easy to make money and make the Heists
irrelevant.

Speaking of making money, by doing things in a certain order when using the
stock market you can make billions of dollars. But you don't want to make too
much money.

There is what is called an integer limit in regards to how your money is
counted. That limit is around $2.1 billion. If you try to go over it will
either freeze on that amount or even turn it into *NEGATIVE* $2.1 billion,
something you obviously don't want. So, if you want to be a billionaire, aim
for the range of $1.5 to $1.8 billion which is way more than you will ever
need.

One other thing about negative numbers. If you are in negative territory and
you sell stock it will not change the amount and the money will disappear.
For example, if you are -$10 and you sell $500,000 in stock you will still
have -$10 and the $500,000 will vanish essentially screwing you out of big
money. So it is important you never get into negative money territory
(although it may be fixed with one of the recent patches).

 /=========================================================================\
| >GEN22. Advanced Tips And Information                                     |
 \=========================================================================/
            \=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=/

Below are some tips and additional information that will be of benefit to 
you:

0===============0
| The White Dots \
0=========================================================>

  As you explore the city of Los Santos you may encounter a random white dot 
  on your radar. These white dots are random people that you can talk to for 
  some interesting conversation. They do not provide any money, weapons, or 
  missions. They are just there to make the city more interesting, nothing 
  more.

0===========================0
| Propane and Gasoline Tanks \
0=========================================================>

  All around the map you may find small and large propane tanks. The small 
  ones are usually red and the larger ones can be either dark red or white. 
  Shooting or even kicking the small ones will cause it to explode. If you 
  shoot a larger one it will shoot out a jet of flame. Shooting it multiple 
  times will cause a large explosion which will definitely bring the Cops.

  You may find large gasoline tanks at gas stations or even being towed on 
  the freeway. You can cause a lot of chaos on the roadway if you blow up one 
  when you pass it by.

0===========0
| Securicars \
0=========================================================>

  These security vans, called the Brute Stockade in this installment can be 
  jacked and blown up to get a few bucks. However, there is a different type 
  of Stockade and that is only available during the Random Events opened 
  later in the game.

| >GEN24. Accomplishments List                                              |
 \=========================================================================/
            \=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=+=/

Listed in this chapter are all of the Accomplishments that can be acquired
in GTA V.

Now, for the sake of terminology and to lessen confusion within this guide,
Accomplishments are what are known as Achievements on the Xbox 360 and PC
versions and Trophies on the PS3 version. To those who do not know,
Achievements and Trophies can be considered a different kind of scoring
system. Each Xbox 360 game has 1000 Achievement Points that can be obtained.

However, the PS3 Trophies do not have a point system attached to them
although the numbers of Trophies attained can be considered a way of keeping
score (as well as add some kind of experience points in the PlayStation
Network system). In addition, the Trophies are split into Bronze, Silver,
Gold and Platinum classes.

Some Accomplishments can be acquired by simply playing through the game.
Others can be obtained by doing certain objectives outside of normal
gameplay. To many gamers this adds to the replay value of each game and gives
them bragging rights on Xbox Live or PlayStation Network where these scores
are posted.

One annoyance to Accomplishments is that, depending on the game, they are
split between Single Player and Multiplayer modes. So, if you do not have the
necessary connections to get on-line, then you most likely cannot get into
multiplayer matches to obtain them.

Unfortunately, GTA V is one of these split Accomplishment games. Even more
annoying is the fact that the Online portion of the game was separate from
the main game and activated two weeks after release.

Many of the Accomplishments within the game are easy to obtain. Some require
more work. They are broken down into Visible Single Player, Secret Single
Player, Multiplayer, and PS3 Specific sections:
